1.w: For the music director, by David, a psalm, a song. God springs into action. His enemies scatter; his adversaries run from him.

2.w: As smoke is driven away by the wind, so you drive them away. As wax melts before fire, so the wicked are destroyed before God.

3.w: But the godly are happy; they rejoice before God and are overcome with joy.

4.w: Sing to God! Sing praises to his name. Exalt the one who rides on the clouds. For the Lord is his name. Rejoice before him.

5.w: He is a father to the fatherless and an advocate for widows. God rules from his holy dwelling place.

6.w: God settles in their own homes those who have been deserted; he frees prisoners and grants them prosperity. But sinful rebels live in the desert.

7.w: O God, when you lead your people into battle, when you march through the wastelands, (Selah)

8.w: the earth shakes. Yes, the heavens pour down rain before God, the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.

9.w: O God, you cause abundant showers to fall on your chosen people. When they are tired, you sustain them,

10.w: for you live among them. You sustain the oppressed with your good blessings, O God.

11.w: The Lord speaks; many, many women spread the good news.

12.w: Kings leading armies run away—they run away! The lovely lady of the house divides up the loot.

13.w: When you lie down among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove are covered with silver and with glittering gold.

14.w: When the Sovereign One scatters kings, let it snow on Zalmon.

15.w: The mountain of Bashan is a towering mountain; the mountain of Bashan is a mountain with many peaks.

16.w: Why do you look with envy, O mountains with many peaks, at the mountain where God has decided to live? Indeed the Lord will live there permanently.

17.w: God has countless chariots; they number in the thousands. The Lord comes from Sinai in holy splendor.

18.w: You ascend on high; you have taken many captives. You receive tribute from men, including even sinful rebels. Indeed, the Lord God lives there.

19.w: The Lord deserves praise. Day after day he carries our burden, the God who delivers us. (Selah)

20.w: Our God is a God who delivers; the Lord , the Sovereign Lord, can rescue from death.

21.w: Indeed, God strikes the heads of his enemies, the hairy foreheads of those who persist in rebellion.

22.w: The Lord says, “I will retrieve them from Bashan. I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,

23.w: so that your feet may stomp in their blood, and your dogs may eat their portion of the enemies’ corpses.”

24.w: They see your processions, O God— the processions of my God, my king, who marches along in holy splendor.

25.w: Singers walk in front; musicians follow playing their stringed instruments, in the midst of young women playing tambourines.

26.w: In your large assemblies praise God, the Lord , in the assemblies of Israel.

27.w: There is little Benjamin, their ruler, and the princes of Judah in their robes, along with the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali.

28.w: God has decreed that you will be powerful. O God, you who have acted on our behalf, demonstrate your power.

29.w: Because of your temple in Jerusalem, kings bring tribute to you.

30.w: Sound your battle cry against the wild beast of the reeds, and the nations that assemble like a herd of calves led by bulls. They humble themselves and offer gold and silver as tribute. God scatters the nations that like to do battle.

31.w: They come with red cloth from Egypt. Ethiopia voluntarily offers tribute to God.

32.w: O kingdoms of the earth, sing to God. Sing praises to the Lord, (Selah)

33.w: to the one who rides through the sky from ancient times. Look! He thunders loudly.

34.w: Acknowledge God’s power, his sovereignty over Israel, and the power he reveals in the skies.

35.w: You are awe inspiring, O God, as you emerge from your holy temple. It is the God of Israel who gives the people power and strength. God deserves praise!
